clue.text: Soldier escort arranged for individually owned businesses

parts.note: a private is the lowest-ranking soldier

indicators.note: things arranged are put into a new order, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier is assigned a bodyguard, arranged on behalf of some independent businesses.
explanation.definitionFit: The private sector is the part of the economy made up of firms owned by people rather than the state.

clue.text: Boar's feet cooked as traditional English fare

indicators.note: cooked food is transformed, and cooked books are falsified, so the letters before are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Pig's trotters prepared in the kitchen are offered up as a classic English dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sunday joint of roasted beef is the dish most associated with English cooking, hence the French nickname les rosbifs.

clue.text: Failing to take the first Orient Express

indicators.note: one word takes in, or holds, another inside itself

parts.note: a failing is a moral fault or vice

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is wanted here

parts.note: the opening letter of Orient

explanation.surface: Someone misses catching the famous luxury train, the Orient Express.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Orient Express' as the train, but 'Express' is the definition, a verb meaning to put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to state or utter it, the verb sense of express.

clue.text: Cheated at pontoon?

parts.note: surface reading: swindled someone during a card game
setter's reading: in pontoon, the call for another card has a name meaning bent out of shape, and bent also means dishonest

explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is the British name for blackjack, where asking for another card is to 'twist'; twisted also means cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: Twisted is informal for swindled or double-crossed, and in pontoon it describes having taken another card.

clue.text: What a heavenly colour!

parts.note: surface reading: an exclamation of delight at a gorgeous shade
setter's reading: literally belonging to the heavens above, the hue of a clear day overhead

explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly' looks like gushing praise, but it is meant literally: the colour of the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky-blue is the pale clear blue of the daytime firmament above us.

clue.text: Dishonest dealer

parts.note: surface reading: a crooked trader or merchant
setter's reading: the person who deals out playing cards at the table

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dealer' suggests business, but the cheat is dealing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A card-sharp is a professional cheat who swindles others at card games.

clue.text: Inaccurate serve results in defeat

parts.note: wide of the mark, as in 'out by a mile'
to serve a purpose is to do, as in 'that will do'

explanation.surface: A tennis player's wayward serve costs them the match.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis picture makes 'serve' a stroke and 'Inaccurate serve' one idea, but each word gives its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo a rival is to surpass or beat them, a verb close to defeat.

clue.text: Outlook splendid, yet tense

parts.note: prospects or outlook, what lies ahead
flawless, splendid

explanation.surface: Prospects look wonderful, yet someone still feels nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as an adjective for anxiety; it is the grammar noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The future perfect is a verb tense, as in 'will have finished', describing an action complete at a later time.

clue.text: Risk playing Russian roulette?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to take a gamble
second meaning, playful: gambling with a revolver held to one's head, an arm being slang for a gun

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means to take a chance, and the question mark admits the pun on arm as a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to attempt something risky, and the roulette player literally gambles with a loaded weapon.

clue.text: Harmony restored in a mutiny

indicators.note: something restored is rebuilt, so the letters that follow are put together again in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Peace is brought back aboard a ship whose crew had rebelled.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that a mutiny is the opposite of harmony, yet its letters make it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unanimity is complete agreement among everyone, which is a state of accord or concord.

clue.text: New chart set up by degrees

definitions.note: names what the device does rather than the device

indicators.note: a new version of something is made afresh, so the following letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh graph is plotted showing temperatures in degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: A ratch is an old word for a ratchet, a toothed mechanism that moves one notch at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet or ratch advances a load notch by notch, raising it step by step.

clue.text: Sort of nut that is loose

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant version, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: Some kind of nut has come loose from its bolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' reads as an adjective about the nut, but it is the verb meaning to unfasten.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose a knot or bond is to undo or unfasten it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Is patronising in speech and overbearing in argument

definitions.meaning: second meaning: silences an opponent by out-arguing them

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to speak condescendingly to someone and to silence them by persistent argument.

clue.text: Chaps caught in foul deed are corrected

indicators.note: one thing caught in another sits trapped inside it
something foul is corrupted or spoilt, so the word after it is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Men caught red-handed in a wicked act are put right.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct its errors, so emended means put right or amended.

clue.text: Measures following cut in naval establishments

indicators.note: coming after another word, so the clue's first word goes second in the order

parts.note: to dock is to cut short, as with a tail or wages
a yard is a measure of length

explanation.surface: Cuts in staff follow new measures at naval bases.
explanation.definitionFit: Dockyards are shipbuilding and repair facilities, many of them run by the navy.

clue.text: Model, formerly fat?

parts.note: ex- means former
ample, plump or well-rounded

explanation.surface: A fashion model who used to be overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests the catwalk, but here it means a pattern to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is something to imitate, a pattern or model for others.

clue.text: Tip or pour out a delightful mixture

indicators.note: out can mean not in order or wrong, so the preceding words are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for emptying a bowl of some pleasant blend.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a scented mix of dried petals, and by extension any medley of assorted items.

clue.text: Radio makes sound use of them

definitions.text: Radio makes sound use of them

parts.note: surface reading: the broadcaster uses something wisely and sensibly
setter's reading: noise, so what is meant is the special noises added to programmes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound use' seems to mean sensible use, but it is about audio.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound effects are the artificial noises, like doors creaking or hooves, that radio drama relies on.

clue.text: A hard blow for the Italians

definitions.text: A hard blow for the Italians

parts.note: surface reading: a severe setback or misfortune
setter's reading: a wind, a fierce one that sweeps over southern Europe

explanation.walkthrough: 'A hard blow' reads as bad news; it is a strong wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot, dusty wind blowing from North Africa across the Mediterranean into Italy.

clue.text: Revolutionary means of power on board

definitions.text: Revolutionary means of power on board

parts.note: surface reading: a radical route to political control in a committee
setter's reading: literally rotating, a turning drum on a ship's deck

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' and 'board' suggest a coup at a meeting; read literally they mean turning on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a rotating vertical drum on a ship used to haul in cables and anchors.

clue.text: Is inclined to enter the Church, subject to purification

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
leans, tilts or is inclined

explanation.surface: Someone feels drawn to become a priest, wanting to be cleansed of sin.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse is to make clean or pure, i.e. to put through a purifying process.

clue.text: Lacking the imagination to fall in love?

definitions.text: Lacking the imagination to fall in love?

parts.note: setter's reading: free of fancy, fancy meaning imagination
surface reading: too unromantic to be swept off one's feet

explanation.walkthrough: Fancy means imagination and also romantic attraction, so being without it leaves one unattached.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy-free describes someone not in love and without commitments, carefree and unattached.

clue.text: Nerve broken? Not at all!

indicators.note: a broken thing is in pieces, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether their courage has cracked replies indignantly that it hasn't.
explanation.definitionFit: Never, said as an exclamation, is an emphatic denial, the same as not at all.

clue.text: They may indicate a safe course for young men, say

definitions.text: They may indicate a safe course

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: young men are boys

explanation.surface: Advice on steering youths along the right path in life.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the floating marker is often pronounced just like 'boys'.
explanation.definitionFit: Buoys are floating markers anchored to show ships the navigable channel.

clue.text: Is extravagant with music

definitions.meaning: first meaning: squanders money, British slang 'blue' as a verb
second meaning: the melancholy African-American genre

explanation.walkthrough: To blue money is old British slang for spending it recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Blues is a verb for wasting cash lavishly and also the name of a musical style from the American South.

clue.text: Chap gets the right sort of insurance

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a chap
R abbreviates right

explanation.surface: A man obtains the appropriate kind of insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance cover is the protection a policy provides, as in fully comprehensive cover.

clue.text: Victor or William, perhaps

definitions.meaning: second meaning: William I of England, who invaded in 1066

explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor or William' looks like a choice of first names; Victor is a winner, and William I was called the Conqueror.
explanation.definitionFit: A conqueror is one who wins by force, and William the Conqueror led the Norman invasion of England.

clue.text: Try to look smart in order to go courting?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, literal: iron a jacket and trousers
second meaning: pursue a romantic proposal

explanation.walkthrough: Pressing clothes means ironing them, while pressing a suit in the old sense means urging a marriage proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: To press one's suit is the old idiom for urging romantic attention on someone, and literally means ironing clothes.
